title: Provenance record
description: Written by every tool, on every run, in an identical shape. Tools stamp their own version and the schema version into this record; nothing here is manually logged, because manual logging is the first thing to rot.

tool.description: What ran. Stamped by the tool itself, never supplied by hand -- manual logging is the first thing to rot. A conforming tool is named tcat-<verb>; anything else must set conforming to false, which is the state every spoke passes through while bootstrapping and every legacy deposit stays in.

name.description: A conforming tool's declared name. To record something else, set conforming: false.

conforming.description: False when this artifact was produced by something that does not implement the tool contract -- a lab conversion script, a spreadsheet, a hand deposit. Recording it as a flag rather than allowing any name silently is what keeps the question answerable: 'what in this store was never produced by a conforming tool?' is a query someone will need at release time, and it must not require reading notes fields to answer. Such an artifact carries no cache guarantee and no reproducibility claim beyond what its notes say.

git_sha.description: Commit of the analysis hub the tool ran from. The literal string 'dirty' is permitted and is the honest answer for a working-tree run; it also disqualifies the artifact from promotion.

spoke.description: The repository implementing this tool, e.g. 'tcat-analysis-coox'. Optional and informational: identity is (name, version) plus git_sha, and two spokes implementing one declared tool should produce identical artifacts -- but a reader tracing a result wants to know WHERE the code lives without parsing free-text notes.

inputs.description: Artifact ids of every input, in the order the tool consumed them. May be empty for a tool that reads only a manifest from disk (tcat-ingest at the raw boundary).

parameters.description: Every parameter that entered the artifact id hash. This is where an applied calibration's interpolation rule is recorded, so that choice is auditable rather than buried in code.

data_schema_version.description: Version of the data standard the tool validated against.

durability.description: Marked at creation, never inferred later. ephemeral = solver checkpoints and intermediate residuals, garbage-collectable, never synced between institutions. durable = fitted parameters, processed datasets, calibrations.

host.description: Machine the tool ran on. Not part of the artifact hash -- the same computation on two machines must produce the same id -- but recorded, because it is the first thing you want when one site's result disagrees with another's.

site.description: Which store this artifact was first written to.

inputs_detail.description: Optional per-input annotation, for when the role of an input is not obvious from its position.

environment.description: Optional. Enough to reconstruct the run if a result is later disputed.

runtime_s.description: Wall-clock seconds. Recorded because the AI-advantage metric is stated in wall-clock terms, so it needs to accumulate as a by-product rather than be reconstructed later.

notes.description: Free text. Where a human explains something the parameters do not, such as why a run was retried.
